Q954886.label: 1979 Canadian federal election
Q954886.desc: creation of the 31st Parliament of the North American country
Q954886.summary: The 1979 Canadian federal election was held on May 22, 1979, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada of the 31st Parliament of Canada. It resulted in the defeat of the Liberal Party of Canada after 16 years in power, 11 of them under Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau. Joe Clark led the Progressive Conservative Party to power but with only a minority of seats in the House of Commons. The Liberals, however, beat the Progressive Conservatives in the overall popular vote by more than 400,000 votes.

Q11270.label: Fulgencio Batista
Q11270.summary: Fulgencio Batista y Zaldívar was a Cuban military officer and politician who served as president of Cuba from 1940 to 1944, from 1952 to 1954 and again from 1955 to his resignation in 1959, when he was overthrown in the Cuban Revolution. From 1934 till 1940 he was the de facto leader of Cuba.

Q881158.label: Juan José Arévalo
Q881158.summary: Juan José Arévalo Bermejo was a Guatemalan statesman and professor of philosophy who became Guatemala's first democratically elected president in 1945. He was elected following a popular uprising against the United States-backed dictator Jorge Ubico that began the Guatemalan Revolution. He remained in office until 1951, surviving 25 coup attempts. He did not contest the election of 1951, instead choosing to hand over power to Jacobo Árbenz. As president, he enacted several social reform policies, including an increase in the minimum wage and a series of literacy programs.

Q136773126.label: Next Dutch general election
Q136773126.summary: General elections are scheduled to be held in the Netherlands on 15 May 2030 to elect the members of the House of Representatives, but may be held at an earlier date if a snap election is called.

Q1970182.label: 2004 Slovak presidential election
Q1970182.summary: Presidential elections were held in Slovakia on 3 April 2004, with a second round on 17 April. Although former Prime Minister Vladimír Mečiar received the most votes in the first round, he was defeated by Ivan Gašparovič in the run-off.

Q587782.label: 1946 Icelandic parliamentary election
Q587782.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 30 June 1946. The Independence Party remained the largest party in the Lower House of the Althing, winning 13 of the 35 seats.

Q49670.label: Progressive Citizens' Party
Q49670.desc: political party in the principality of Liechtenstein
Q49670.summary: The Progressive Citizens' Party in Liechtenstein is a conservative political party in Liechtenstein. The FBP is one of the two major political parties in Liechtenstein, along with the liberal-conservative Patriotic Union. Founded in 1918 along with the now-defunct Christian-Social People's Party, it is the oldest extant party in Liechtenstein.

Q7174.label: democracy
Q7174.desc: system in which sovereignty resides in the people and their will is reflected in governance
Q7174.summary: Democracy is a form of government in which political power is vested in the people of a certain state. Under a narrow definition of democracy, rulers are elected through competitive elections, while broader definitions also link democracy to guarantees of civil liberties and human rights.
